The people who are mainly served by this wharf are the people in the Grand River district, and the petition of 1921 which caused the government to take action was largely signed by the people of Grand River district. They wanted that wharf, and they want the wharf that exists to-day. It is only the few who have a piece of property at the lower end of Soldiers' Cove who want this new wharf-a wharf, mind you, to reach which the people will have to go one and a half miles further. As the petition says:
Whereas the present site of the wharf at Soldier's Cove is most easy of access

The people who are to be served say that the present wharf is most easy of access. The petition goes on:
We further petition your department to effect the necessary repairs to the present wharf, which we consider would be of greater service to the community which it serves and a great saving to the treasury of this dominion.
In 1921 this same engineer, Mr. Locke, investigated both sites through his resident engineer, and when no political pressure was being exerted, he selected the site on which the present wharf is built and recommended that to the department, but to-day on account of the little 'bit of political pressure that has been exerted by my opponent in the last election, and by one or two people who want to make a little divvy out of the sale of a piece of land, this government throws discretion to the winds. Our fishing communities need the expenditure of public money on every part of the Atlantic seaboard, and all they are asking for in this case is a little

bit of repairs to the present wharf. Owing to the action of provincial government officials in 1925 the old wharf was broken, and this government has never seen fit to repair it. There was an item in the estimates of 1926 for repairing that wharf, but this government did not see fit to expend that money when they came back into power, and to-day we find in the estimates an item of $4,200 for the building of a new wharf in a different locality altogether. As the representative of that community, as the one who receives the large support of that district and the support of the adjoining districts, I make the statement here that I am opposed to that sort of public expenditure. I want public money expended for public service, and not to gratify a few barnacles that are hanging on to this government.

speakerposition: Deputy Speaker and Chair of Committees of the Whole of the House of Commons
speechtext: Shall the item carry?

No. I move to amend the item by striking out the words "wharf replacement" and substituting therefor the words "repairs to present wharf." It may be necessary to reduce the amount from $4,200. I am opposed to this item absolutely.

The house has no doubt been impressed by the excellent case presented by the hon. member who has just taken his seat, and although I know nothing about the situation my curiosity has been aroused, and I would ask the minister to explain the situation, or to answer the allegations that have been made by the hon. gentleman.
I did not notice whether my hon. friend was in his seat when I made the explanation in regard to this item. If he was, I suppose he heard me.
I am sorry I did not catch what the minister said.

I gave a full explanation, but I shall be glad to give it again. This is not a new matter. It has been a matter of controversy in that community since this wharf was first proposed in the year 1902, and there has been a serious difference of opinion with regard to it. For that reason a very careful examination was made and greater care was taken in ascertaining the relative merits of the two sites than otherwise would have been the case.

Will the minister explain how it happens that a report evidently came from the engineer three or four years ago in

Supply-Harbours and Rivers, N.S.
favour of one site, and now another report comes from the same engineer in favour of a different site. I should be glad if the minister would elucidate that.
The first recommendation was in favour of the site that we now propose.
By the same engineer?

I take exception to the minister's statement. In 1902 there was no such thing as a wharf in that district. I have been practising medicine for fifteen years in that community, and I take exception to the minister's statement.
If my hon. friend was following me-
I have the floor, and I am going to keep it.
You have not. You gave it up and the minister took it.

I have
as much right to it as the hon. Minister of Railways.

I rise to a ' point of order, Mr. Chairman. I asked the hon. minister a question, and I thought he was doing his best to answer it. He had reached a comparison between the statement of the engineer a few years ago and his statement of to-day. I think he ought to be permitted to conclude his statement, and then I shall be delighted to hear the hon. member for Richmond-West Cape Breton finish his oration.

I was stating that this
is an old controversy, and if my hon. friend from the riding had been paying attention to what I was saying, he would know perfectly well that I did not say there was a wharf there in 1902. I said that there had been an agitation- between two contending parties in that riding as to the best site, each side wanting their own site ever since 1902. My information is that when the people of Soldier's Cove discovered it was proposed to reconstruct the wharf they started an agitation to build a new wharf at another location, the reasons for the change being: (1) The present wharf was at one end of the district, while the proposed site would be in the centre; (2) that when the present wharf was built the majority of the local people were in favour of having it at the site of the now proposed wharf; (3) and that the objection that the then highway was too far away from the site has now been overcome by the provincial main highway coming closer to
the site through a deviation along the shore.
I hope hon. members will not think that this decision was arrived at without the most careful consideration. One cost 84,200; the other will cost over 85,000. My hon. friend will not contend for a moment that the old wharf is suitable at the present time, or that it does not need complete reconstruction at the expenditure that I have stated. Those are the circumstances. The department takes full responsibility, and has arrived at this judgment after the most careful consideration.

The hon. member's
motion is in direct conflict with standing order 56, section 510:
It is not allowable to attach a condition or an expression of opinion to a resolution in the committee of supply, or to change the destination of a grant.

Mr. Chairman, the minister states that an agitation had been conducted since 1902. No doubt when his party was in power from 1902 to 1911 the same people were interviewing the government and doing their utmost to have a wharf built in a locality where only one or two families lived. In 1921 the public placed before the government a petition, signed, as is the present petition, by 153 residents of the district. As a result of the petition the Department of Public Works, through this very same engineer, Mr. Locke, selected the site of the present wharf in Soldier's Cove. I may state that he selected it without political pressure being exerted, as is stated in the petition. Political pressure had been exerted, and was effective for fifteen or twenty years in preventing the wharf being built in that district. There is now a wharf at Soldier's Cove, and it will not take very much money to repair it. The top is in perfect repair; but in 1921 the Department of Public Works, through its engineer, used ordinary native wood instead of creosoted timber.
What year?

1921.
You cannot say that the engineer is bad from the political standpoint, for he has been as good a tool of this government as any that I have ever known. Now, Mr. Chairman, as the representative of that district, thoroughly conversant with every step that has been taken in the construction of this wharf, and knowing the interests that it must serve, I strongly object to the minister's statement. If we do our duty to-day we will repair the present wharf at Soldier's Cove and not incur this additional expense. Instead of handing out public money to a few of his heelers, I

Supply-Harbours and Rivers, N.S.
would ask the minister to extend some of it on wharves along the coast for the benefit of our fishermen; I would ask him to spend it in the opening up of the Grand river; I would ask him to spend it in building a public wharf at Louisburg, or in aiding the districts of Main a Dieu and the Lorraines, L'Ardoise, and so on; I would ask him to spend it in giving us a life saving station at Scatarie island.

As I
understand it, wre are going to spend $4,200 in the purchase of a site to construct a half mile of highway and build a wharf; and the wharf will be built at a point which is not feasible. The first name on the petition to which I have referred is that of a Shipper, the only man who ships out of that port, and in his opinion and in the opinion of the others the site is not feasible. It is a most unusual
occurrence for a representative of a maritime riding to get up and ask for a vote to be reduced, and I am sure the hon. minister, after the many statements he has made in the last few days as to the amount of sweat he has lost in securing money from this wonderful treasury board, should welcome an opportunity to accept the suggestion offered by the hon. member for Richmond-Wegt Cape Breton (Mr. Macdonald). what the estimate consists of? I know nothing about the matter, but I should like to know what the estimate is for the right of way as well as for the wharf itself.

Supply-Harbours and Rivers, N.S.
Yes; we have all the data including the correspondence and-

In view of the stand the minister has taken I want to ask this question:	Is he in favour of
repairing the present wharf which the government built in 1921?

No.

No provision made for
the highway leading up to it?

We have nothing to do
with the roads. A road has been built by the province which comes near the site of the new wharf, but we have made no expenditure in connection with it.

become the provincial highway, and is closer to the wharf.

I will probably drop it
altogether; I do not want to force a wharf on people who do not want it.

The
minister has received a petition signed by 153 people, including the Liberal counsellor in the district of Grand River, asking that the wharf at Soldier's Cove be repaired. This wharf was built as a public convenience and for the public service, and I state distinctly to the committee that the proposed new wharf would not be of public service and would not serve the community. government allowed a provincial government to destroy in 1925 by placing upon it some 50 or 100 tons of sand. This money has been appropriated by the treasury board, and it is the duty of the minister to give those 153 people the public service which they require. I am very much obliged
to my hon. friend for the information he has given and for the manner in which he has given it. in all these cases.

cases. At whose request would the engineer go to Tangier? There are 150 coves and harbours in the county of Halifax; why should they pick out Tangier?

It is the duty of the
engineer to go round to the various wharves and inspect them. They make reports, and from these reports and all the other information which we can obtain we come to the best conclusion possible with regard to the necessity for repairs or construction.

Tangier happens to be sixty miles east of the city of Halifax, and I wonder why the resident engineer of Halifax or the province of Nova Scotia should particularly
pick out that place. I am not saying that Tangier is not an important settlement, but there are others just as important in the constituency of Halifax. I cannot understand why the engineers should pick out that place, sixty miles from Halifax, and find there a necessity for a $1,300 expenditure.

Our report is that this
work is required for the maintenance of the structure which provides facilities for a fishing industry valued at $15,000 annually. Fishing is the only means of support for a population of 400 people. If my hon. friend objects to it, I am willing to let this item drop.

I do not object to the item. My hon. friends say "drop it", but let me tell my hon. friends from the province of Quebec that they are feeding out of the public trough to a greater extent than the province of Nova Scotia.

I suggest to my hon.
friend that he is spending more than the wharf would cost by taking up the time of the committee for half an hour on an item of $1,300.

I have the utmost respect
for the hon. member for Levis (Mr. Dussault), but while we may be on a very small item of $1,300, my hon. friends from the province of Quebec will be talking about $8,500,000 worth, and they will fight very hard for it. I am not objecting to the principle, nor am I objecting to this vote.
I would not say that you are supporting it.
I am supporting it.
We cannot see it yet.

Why is there such a small
vote for the constituency of Halifax? Why should we get $1,300 for Tangier, and not get more in other districts? There have been many requests made for the county of Halifax, and they have not been granted. I cannot understand why this particular district has been picked out for an expenditure of $1,300. I would like to know who requested the engineer to go down there?
If my friend-

I am asking a question of
the Minister of Public Works and my hon. friend from Temiscouata (Mr. Pouliot) may keep his seat.
Item stands.
2956	COMMONS
Supply-Harbours and Rivers, N.S.
Westport-wharf repairs, $3,500.	.

I am very glad to see that
the minister has a small appropriation for this very much needed wharf.

I hope my hon. friend is
not going to insist on this item standing, because I will have to meet his wishes if he does.

I just want to find out
whether this will include some dredging that is needed at this breakwater. It is a very important breakwater.

There is no dredging included in this; it is to cover repairs to the wharf. Our report is that the repairs will consist of rebuilding a section of the pile wharf, 90 feet by 30 feet, on which the piling has been destroyed and eaten off by the limnoria; replacing 30 brace and fender piles, also destroyed, and 10,000 feet board measure of bulkhead. This is one of the most important fishing centres in Digby county, the annual value of the fishing catch amounting to between $200,000 and $300,000. On account of this report, we feel that the repairs should be done, and that they are all needed.

This is a very valuable
breakwater, and a lot of money has been spent on the construction of it. It needs these repairs very badly, but the appropriation now made is totally inadequate. This is a large piece of work, and there is some dredging that is very urgently needed. I hope the minister will give instructions to his resident engineer that a dredge be sent there during this coming summer. Perhaps this can be provided for out of the $65,000 for harbours and rivers generally. I hope the minister will give the necessary instructions to have this work carried out as quickly as possible.

I may say that there is some money being expended out of the general vote to repair the incline slip, bulkhead, refoot some of the piling that was destroyed by the limnoria, and make the wharf 6afe and secure for the winter. This amounts to about $550, and will somewhat increase the amount. Apparently it is a necessary work at a very important point.
I am sure it would be in the public interest if the minister would recommend to the engineer that the necessary dredging be done there.

I shall be very glad to
look into it.

Item agreed to.

Yarmouth bar [DOT]- breakwater repairs and improvements, $4,000.
I presume that has been recommended by the district engineer.
Certainly.
Without any suggestion from the representative of that county.
I could not say as to that.
I thought that would be the answer.

I want to correct the statement I made a short time ago in reference to the expenditure under this vote No. 134, in the counties of Antigonish-Guys-borough and Yarmouth. I stated that there was about $60,000 voted for these two counties, but I find, on going carefully over the figures, that out of nearly $500,000 these two counties are getting $135,800, or 27 per cent of the whole vote. Halifax county, the most populous in the province of Nova Scotia, does not get $16,000, as I said, but $8,500. I would ask the Minister of Public Works not to hold up that item for Tangier, because it would reduce the $8,500 to about $7,200, and that would look very small. I feel that the minister would almost be ashamed of such a small amount.

When my hon. friend was making his estimate I am sure that he wanted to be absolutely fair and not leave the impression that on account of the riding being represented by some particular party it was being discriminated against.

Oh, no, I just
took the figures as they were.
Did my hon. friend take the trouble to see how much was being expended in Queens-Lunenburg? Does he know that about $120,000 is being expended in that riding?
It is needed.
I have no doubt it is. It is because it is needed that it is being spent.
I am not opposing that vote.
It is being spent because our reports show that it is a little more needed there than in the riding represented by my hon. friend.

I want to say a word in answer to the suggestion made by the senior member for Halifax, namely, that public money spent in Nova Scotia should be op-

Supply-Harbours and Rivers, P.E.I.
portioned in proportion to the population or something of that sort. If we adopt that suggestion we shall be following an entirely wrong principle. The money should be spent in accordance with the needs of the various constituencies. There is a feeling in Nova Scotia that a good deal of money is spent in the county of Halifax. We in the other parts of Nova Scotia do not object to that if the money is needed; but it is an entirely erroneous doctrine to be propounded in the house that because the constituency of Halifax does not get a very large proportion in any particular year of the money spent in Nova Scotia, something is wrong. I, as a representative of one of the rural constituencies of Nova Scotia, wish to protest against the idea going out that we from that province are always trying to get all the money we possibly can regardless of the needs of our various constituencies.

Item agreed to.
Prince Edward Island-harbours and rivers-[DOT] Bonshaw freight shed, $2,900.
Why is this freight shed needed?

This is to construct a freight shed, 30 feet by 60 feet. Warehouse facilities are urgently required on account of the development of the seed potato industry in the district. The annual business over the wharf is between $30,000 and $40,000.

Item agreed to.
Charlottetown - reconstruction of railway wharf, $140,000.
Is this wharf being taken over from the railway department by the Public Works department?

An order in council was passed on October 19, 1927, granting authority to transfer from the Canadian National Railways to the Department of Public Works certain wharf properties including the railway wharf, freight shed and portion of coal shed at Charlottetown.

Item agreed to.
West Point wharf repairs, $4,000.

Before the items for Prince Edward Island are all through, while I do not like to follow the suggestions that were made in the house this afternoon and evening with regard to favouritism in .the matter of distributing the money in the Public Works department, yet having regard to the situation that existed last year and that exists this year in Prince Edward Island, I feel it is almost impossible to get
away from that idea. A year ago I drew the minister's attention to the fact that out of an amount of $107,000 voted for harbours and rivers for the three counties of Prince Edward Island, the sum of $1,000, which was a revote from the year before, was voted for Kings county. This year I find a similar condition existing although not to quite so bad an extent. Out of a total vote of $229,800, an amount of $13,000 is voted for Kings county. It seems to one representing the county in opposition and remembering that the other counties have government representation, that our county is being penalized because two years ago it voted against the government. I hate to make that suggestion. I know the minister does not want to play that kind of politics, but it is pretty difficult, in view of the facts as we find them, to entertain any other idea. If we did not have needs, and very serious needs, I would not say a word, but I want to call the attention of the minister to this fact. In 1925 a vote of $36,500 was put through the house for a very important piece of work, namely for the strengthening of the Souris' breakwater. Souris is one of the most important towns in Kings county and it is an important point serving a large section of the people. As I say, in the session of 1925 an amount of $36,500 was voted for this' work and a contract was let, but for some reason or another the contractor did not perform the work. In the session of 1926 the appropriation was dropped; the contract was not renewed and the work has not yet been done. The breakwater is in imminent danger of going to pieces, and if this occurred Souris property would be destroyed. I should like to ask the minister why the vote of $36,500 passed in the session of 1925 was dropped and not renewed, in view of the fact that he has the government engineer's report of the urgent need of the work and the imminent danger of the breakwater being destroyed if it is not strengthened.
Do I understand my hon. friend, who is the representative for Kings county, to say that there was just $1,000 expended in that constituency a year ago?
I said that out of the votes passed in the house a year ago, amounting to $107,000 for harbours and rivers in the whole province, the sum of $1,000 was earmarked for Kings' county.

If my memory serves me aright, an amount of $SI0,000 was expended on a potato warehouse on a wharf in Kings county, my hon. friend's riding, which he says was discriminated against.
2958	COMMONS
Supply-Harbours and Rivers, P.E.I.

I was not
speaking about the votes which were the result, of the recommendations of the Duncan commission. As a result of the recommendations of that commission there were three votes, one for Prince, one for Kings and one for Queens. I was leaving those out altogether because they are not ordinary votes by this parliament. I was referring to the votes for harbours and rivers for the three counties, and for that reason I did not take into account any particular county.

If my hon. friend wishes
to be fair, does he mean to suggest that Kings county last year and this year has not been very generously treated by the Department of Public Works?	.
I may say, Mr. Chairman-
I am not asking you.

I will reply to the minister's question, by asking him another. Does he think it is fair when he votes 8170,000 for the three counties for harbours and rivers generally that only $1,000 should be granted to my county, which needs public works even more than the other counties? I say this to the minister, and he should know it, that in our county we have a larger proportion of harbours and rivers than in any other county in the province.

My hon. friend sees, does
he not, that $145,000 of this $229,000 is a revote?

I am aware of that. I have asked the minister a direct question twice about the Souris breakwater, but I will repeat it. In the session of 1925 this government voted $36,500 for the purpose of strengthening the Souris breakwater. That work was needed at that time, and it has been needed ever since. A contract was let by the government, but through some inadvertence the contractor did not complete his work. The vote was dropped in 1926 and again in 1927. That work is very much needed, because there is imminent danger of the breakwater being destroyed if it is not strengthened. Why was that vote put in the estimates in 1925 and then dropped, and why is it not being renewed now when there is very much greater need for the work?

I suppose the various
officials who have had to pass upon these votes from time to time have decided that something else was more urgent. That is all that I can say.

Does the
minister expect me to be satisfied with suppositions? If so, he is making a mistake. I am not satisfied to take what he supposes at all, and it is not fair to ask a member to accept his suppositions in the matter. If anything could most strongly bear out the charge of favouritism and discrimination against Kings county it is that one fact that a vote was put in for this work when the county was represented by a Liberal, and dropped out of the estimates the following year when he failed to secure re-election, and the vote has been dropped ever since. The minister's answer is not satisfactory. I want something better than that; I want some facts.

I should not like the
impression to go abroad that Kings county had been discriminated against in any way by the other members from the province. I know my hon. friend from Kings wants to be fair to the representatives of Queens and Prince. At all times I have endeavoured personally to co-operate and do anything I could to help the people of Kings county. I want that distinctly understood. When construction of a warehouse at Georgetown was mooted last year we did everything we could to support that request. Even from a selfish point of view, Mr. Chairman, jt was our duty to do what we could to establish a warehouse at that point, because Georgetown harbour is open very much later in the season than Charlottetown harbour, and a considerable quantity of our potatoes and other produce going forward must be shipped through that port. Therefore, as I say, it was essential that we should push for Georgetown if only from a selfish point of view. I think my hon. friend from Kings would not want the impression to go abroad that my colleagues and myself from Prince Edward Island were in any way responsible for votes not being put in the estimates for his county. Kings county needs ' more money, Mr. Chairman, and I think there should be more warehouses established there, because the potato business is growing very rapidly, and I feel sure if the minister can see his way clear to do anything for Kings county next year, or even in the supplementary estimates this year, my colleagues and myself will be only too pleased. I am quite sure that the member for Kings would not want to convey the impression that we were endeavouring to block expenditures for his county. Personally I say from the floor of this house that I am not doing so. On the contrary, I repeat that my colleagues and I

Live Stock Act
are endeavouring in every way to co-operate with the people of Kings county. I only make that statement in order that my position may be clear before the people of my province.
I want to thank the Minister of Public Works for the consideration he has given to our province. A great deal of fault has been found with him to-night, but I sincerely appreciate all he has done for our county, for the building of a wharf at Charlottetown, and numerous other works throughout the province, all of which were necessary. I am sorry to hear so much criticism of the Public Works department because, speaking personally I have always found the minister a first-rate fellow. He is willing to meet any reasonable demand. Our friends on the other side must remember that a great deal of money is being spent in places where we have not representation in accord with the government, notably in Toronto, for instance, and I thi*k the minister has 'been very fair to constituencies that did not send representation to this side of the house. I have always found him very reasonable and wish to add my word of tribute for the good work he is doing.

I would not say a word at
this stage of the debate but for an interjection of the Minister of Public Works when I was endeavouring to answer a question. He said that the had not asked me the question which I attempted to answer on behalf of twenty-five per cent of the representation from Prince Edward Island. The last speaker, who represents part of seventy-five per cent of the representation of Prince Edward Island, has tried to point out that the Department of Public Works has been very fair, but I ask was the minister fair when he tried to place to the credit of Kings county an expenditure of $60,000? May I say, and my friends to the right of the Minister of Public Works will bear me out in this, that Kings county is the only county in Prince Edward Island whose harbours are open to shipping throughout the winter, and naturally a cold storage potato warehouse would be placed in that county. Now when this expenditure is made in Kings county to look after the shipping requirements of the whole province, why should the minister endeavour to place that expenditure to the credit of Kings county?

I was glad to hear the remarks of my hon. friend from Queens (Mr. Jenkins). I wish to assure him
that there was no intention on my part to charge either him or any of his colleagues from Queens or Prince with being a party to discriminating against Queens county. I want to be fair to them because I have always found them absolutely fair with me. But certainly the votes that have gone through the house to-night are not fair to the Island, nor were the votes that were passed last year. With regard to the frostproof warehouse which the minister referred to as having been built in Kings county last fall, I think the remarks of the member for Queens make it clear that that was not a county affair, but provincial. I wish to express the appreciation of the people of Kings county for the building. It was late in the season before the contract was let, but from December up to the 4th of January five large steamers loaded at the warehouse. I think this justifies the expenditure. But I do wish to get an answer from the minister in regard to the vote for the Souris breakwater which was placed in the estimates, passed by the house, and the contract let in 1925. Why has not the work been carried on since?

Mr. Chairman, I move
that the committee rise and report progress
Progress reported.

maintopic: LIVE STOCK AND LIVE STOCK PRODUCTS ACT

speechtext:
The house in committee on Bill No. 61, to amend the Live Stock and Live Stock Products Act-Mr. Motherwell-Mr. Johnston in the chair.
On section 1-Regulations-Beef for domestic consumption.

maintopic: LIVE STOCK AND LIVE STOCK PRODUCTS ACT
speechtext:
Will the minister explain
the bill?

speakeroldname: Hon. W. R. MOTHERWELL (Minister of Agriculture):
maintopic: LIVE STOCK AND LIVE STOCK PRODUCTS ACT
speechtext:
Mr. Chairman, this is a bill
to provide for the voluntary grading of beef for domestic consumption. It is the result of the work of a committee that entered very fully into the whole question throughout western Canada. They also visited Chicago to ascertain how the grading system was working there. As a result they recommended that this system of voluntary grading should be adopted. Their recommendation was endorsed by the Western Canada Live stock Union. The 'bill passed through the committee on agriculture without change, and at this hour of the night I can safely recommend it to the consideration of the house.
29G0
Live Stock Act

maintopic: LIVE STOCK AND LIVE STOCK PRODUCTS ACT
speechtext: Does the minister suggest that it would not be all right in the morning?

maintopic: LIVE STOCK AND LIVE STOCK PRODUCTS ACT
speechtext: It would be all right both morning and evening.

maintopic: LIVE STOCK AND LIVE STOCK PRODUCTS ACT
speechtext:
Are you adopting the
United States stripe system of branding?

maintopic: LIVE STOCK AND LIVE STOCK PRODUCTS ACT
speechtext: That was discussed in the report, and it was thought to be a very handy way. I may say that we are not accepting in toto the recommendations of the committee to which I have referred. We propose to call together all parties who are interested in the grading of beef, that is, a representative butcher, a representative abattoir man, and a representative producer, in order to work out the grades. It is important to ascertain just how many grades are required. The committee recommended that there be two grades only-choice and fancy. There is a difference of opinion whether those would be suitable names. To make quite sure that that is what the country desires one of the first steps to be taken will be to call together, as I have said, a fully representative committee of all the various interests, and so work out a system of grades.

maintopic: LIVE STOCK AND LIVE STOCK PRODUCTS ACT
speechtext:
Have the United States
added a third grade yet?

maintopic: LIVE STOCK AND LIVE STOCK PRODUCTS ACT
speechtext: I do not think so.

maintopic: LIVE STOCK AND LIVE STOCK PRODUCTS ACT
speechtext:
Has it worked out fairly
successfully in the United States?
Mr. MOTHERW'ELL: It seems so. Some are not enthusiastic over there, but I think the system has come to stay. There seems to be, a very general opinion in favour of it, especially in western Canada. I found a much greater number of people supporting th,e system than I anticipated, especially the small butchers, who find it necessary in the summer time to order their meat from the abattoirs. They never know what they are getting. Under this system they would order by name the grade they want, and if not supplied they would have some redress against the abattoir.

maintopic: LIVE STOCK AND LIVE STOCK PRODUCTS ACT
speechtext:
I do not think you need
the system so much to protect the dealer- he is a pretty good judge of beef-as the consumer, who when he ordered prime steer beef steak was sold cow beef of second quality. Cut up into steaks, he could not tell what grade was being supplied. With this system of branding in force the grade will be indicated, no matter how thin the steak may be. In that way the consumer will be educated to buy the better grades. This will have

beneficial effect on the producer, inasmuch as he will receive a little more for first class beef. That has been the great trouble all the way through-the ability of the middleman to sell second or third grade steer beef for first class. I notice this simply gives you power to work out your system later on.

maintopic: LIVE STOCK AND LIVE STOCK PRODUCTS ACT
speechtext: Yes.

maintopic: LIVE STOCK AND LIVE STOCK PRODUCTS ACT
speechtext: I am a little disappointed, Mr. Chairman, that the minister now intimates that the form which the brand is to take is to be left open. In committee we were advised that the roller system would foe adopted. I hope he is not going to retire from the position then taken and that possibly the stamp system may be adopted. This would not cover every cut of beef, and, as the member for Victoria (Mr. Tolmie) points out, it is the public that must be protected.

maintopic: LIVE STOCK AND LIVE STOCK PRODUCTS ACT
speechtext: After this committee works out a system of grades which* it is prepared to recommend, such system will first of all foe submitted to the trade, and to the consumers and producers, to see how acceptable it will be. It will have to be done quickly, on the roller system, just as we brand the top of a box of butter. It is the same system. We shall have to work out some system and submit it to the interested public and find out whether they have any suggestions to- offer before it- is finally adopted.

maintopic: LIVE STOCK AND LIVE STOCK PRODUCTS ACT
speechtext: That is all I wanted to know. The bill is a good one and I approve of it. The minister is of the opinion that the roller system is a good one?

maintopic: LIVE STOCK AND LIVE STOCK PRODUCTS ACT
speechtext: Yes; it is the most expeditious.

maintopic: LIVE STOCK AND LIVE STOCK PRODUCTS ACT
speechtext:
The minister probably
knows already that a considerable number of cattle are being slaughtered in some provinces and are reacting from the tuberculin test. How will he indicate beef of that character?

maintopic: LIVE STOCK AND LIVE STOCK PRODUCTS ACT
speechtext:
That opens up a
considerable problem which we can more properly discuss on the vote for the administration of the Health of Animals Act.

maintopic: LIVE STOCK AND LIVE STOCK PRODUCTS ACT
speechtext:
Is not this a good time
to take it up?

Section agreed to.
Bill reported, read the third time and passed.
On motion of Mr. Lapointe the house adjourned at 10.55 p.m.
